title: Send Your Name to Saturn's Largest Moon
summary:
NASA will send a robot helicopter to Titan, the largest of Saturn's 292 moons, and your name can ride along.

Dragonfly, with eight blades, is planned to launch no earlier than July 2028 and reach Titan in 2034 after six years of travel.

NASA has opened an online list for names to be put on a tiny chip aboard Dragonfly. People who sign up will get a digital boarding pass. The names will not help run the mission, but Nicky Fox, NASA's Science Mission Directorate associate administrator, said NASA is excited to bring humanity along.

Titan has dunes above lakes and rivers of methane, and a surface near minus 290 degrees Fahrenheit. Yet an ocean hides under its icy shell, and scientists think it may hold building blocks for life, but no one can be sure without going there.

After landing, Dragonfly will hop to places during a three-year mission, traveling 70 miles and visiting 20 to 30 areas to look for signs life could exist. Sign-ups close at 11:59 p.m. EST on January 15, 2027.
why_it_matters: You could sign up and get a digital boarding pass showing your name is riding on a real space mission to a faraway moon.
